draws.answer: To execute a query, the database engine first compiles the SQL code, parsing it to ensure proper semantics and verifying that referenced database objects exist and that the user has appropriate access. The SQL is then converted into bytecode, which describes the steps needed on the database engine in an efficient, machine-readable way. The query optimizer analyzes this bytecode to decide how best to execute the query, potentially reordering and refactoring steps for optimal resource use. Finally, the query is executed, and results are produced.

Time series is a series of values organized by time. In [Ch. 5], it is described as "A time series is a series of values organized by time. For example, stock prices might move as trades are executed throughout the day, or a weather sensor will take atmospheric temperatures every minute. Any events that are recorded over time—either regularly or sporadically—are time-series data. A time-series database is optimized for retrieving and statistical processing of time-series data."
Asked as: "What is Time Series?"

Micro-batching is a way to process data in small chunks or batches, typically every two minutes to every second. Some micro-batch frameworks are designed for this use case and will perform well with appropriately allocated resources at a high batch frequency. Micro-batching involves taking a subset of data from a source system, based either on a time interval or the size of accumulated data.

Streaming data processing is inherently more complicated than batch, and the tools and paradigms are arguably less mature. As streaming data becomes more pervasive in every stage of the data engineering lifecycle, data engineers face interesting software engineering problems. For instance, data processing tasks such as joins that we take for granted in the batch processing world often become more complicated in real time, requiring more complex software engineering. Engineers must also write code to apply a variety of windowing methods. Windowing allows real-time systems to calculate valuable metrics such as trailing statistics. Engineers have many frameworks to choose from, including various function platforms (OpenFaaS, AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions) for handling individual events or dedicated stream processors (Spark, Beam, Flink, or Pulsar) for analyzing streams to support reporting and real-time actions.

Batch processing is about ingesting data in large chunks either on a predetermined time interval or as data reaches a preset size threshold. Once data is broken into batches, the latency for downstream consumers is inherently constrained. Streaming ingestion allows for continuous, real-time data delivery to downstream systems with latency less than one second after data is produced.
Asked as: "What is batch vs streaming?"

draws.asked_as: What is benefits of data meshs?
draws.answer:
Data mesh fundamentally changes how data is served within an organization by decentralizing responsibility. Each domain team takes on two aspects: serving data to other teams by preparing it for consumption, and potentially running dashboards and analytics for self-service. This means that instead of siloed data teams, every domain team is responsible for both internal and external data management.
Asked as: "What is benefits of data meshs?"
